title: IHIT Identifies Man Killed in Vancouver Police Shooting
article: Police have now released the identity of the Vancouver man shot to death after brandishing a knife at his wife during a domestic dispute. Eugene Anthony Knight was apparently holding a knife to the throat of his 46-year-old wife. Non-police witnesses confirmed that police asked him to drop the knife and he didn't. He was tasered and he didn't and then he was shot.

On September 18, 2009 at approximately 9:30pm three Vancouver City Police Officers responded to a 911 domestic violence call. Officers arrived at 102-2572 Birch Street within four minutes and forced entry thru the suite door encountering a man later identified as 46 year old Eugene Anthony Knight holding a knife to the throat of his 46 year old wife.

Officers were heard by civilian witnesses to have issued verbal commands to drop the knife. A Conducted Energy Weapon (Taser) was subsequently deployed by an officer with 18 years service with the VPD which proved to be ineffective. Two of the Officers with 10 yrs and 9 months service with the VPD then discharged their firearms fatally wounding Knight.
Knights wife was not physically harmed and was transported to the Vancouver Police office along with her 13 year old daughter who was present in the home at the time of this incident.
Victim's assistance has been provided to both mother and daughter.

IHIT has been delegated the independent lead investigative responsibility by request and with support from the Vancouver Police Department. The Office of the Public Complaints Commission has also been engaged in this investigation.
